candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — implementation of maternal patient safety bundles
candidate.educational_objective: Implement maternal patient safety bundles as evidence-informed, standardized quality-improvement frameworks that are adapted to local resources while preserving individualized clinical assessment and treatment.

options.A: Use the bundle’s evidence-informed actionable practices, adapt implementation to the facility’s resources and setting, and standardize the agreed process within the institution while preserving patient-specific clinical judgment.
options.B: Treat every bundle element as an inflexible national order set that must be applied identically in every facility and to every patient.
options.C: Use the bundle only for patients already known to be high risk because patient safety bundles are not intended to improve general systems of maternal care.
options.D: Replace ongoing clinical assessment and individualized treatment decisions with the bundle checklist once implementation begins.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. Current AIM guidance defines patient safety bundles as collections of evidence-informed best practices developed by multidisciplinary experts to improve processes of care and outcomes for clinically specific conditions in pregnant and postpartum patients. Bundles contain actionable steps that can be adapted to different facilities and resource levels. AIM also states that bundle guidance is not meant to dictate an exclusive course of treatment; local adaptation is appropriate, while standardization within an institution is strongly encouraged. B falsely makes the bundle inflexible across settings. C incorrectly limits systems-based safety work to patients already labeled high risk. D misuses a quality-improvement framework as a substitute for bedside assessment and individualized clinical judgment.
candidate.source_claim_supported: AIM patient safety bundles provide evidence-informed, actionable practices that can be adapted to local resources and standardized within an institution; they support but do not replace individualized clinical judgment or dictate one exclusive treatment course.
